newsitem.title: CHILE: El Abra mine to work while belt unearthed.
newsitem.headline: El Abra mine to work while belt unearthed.

text.p: The El Abra mine and ore processing facilities will continue operating while workers dig out tonnes of debris left on the conveyor belt after a tunnel caved in Wednesday, the mine's spokesman said.

The mine was still evaluating the impact of the accident, in which four workers died, on production but the ore crusher and heap leaching plants could continue working with stockpiles, said spokesman Marcelo Nunez.
"We've got quite a bit of material in stock, but nor will it last that long," he said, adding that he could not be more specific.
He had no information on whether the mine would be able to make its copper delivery commitments, some of which were signed before the mine began making cathodes in August, he said.

The mine, owned by Cyprus Amax Minerals, is due to hit full production of 225,000 tonnes sometime in 1997. A Cyprus Amax spokesman in Denver said earlier he did not think the mine's delivery commitments would be affected by the accident.
